evals.name: pytest-two-signatures
evals.prompt: tests/test_cache.py::test_cache_hit fails sometimes in CI but passes when I run it locally. is it actually flaky? how often does it fail and what does the failure look like? don't fix it yet
evals.expected_output: Runs the test many times, reports a failure rate (~35-60%), and distinguishes two signatures: the hits assertion (TTL expiry) and TimeoutError from fetch_remote.
expectations: The test was executed at least 10 times (a loop, repetition tool, or script), not just once or twice
The final answer reports a numeric failure count or rate out of the total number of runs
The final answer distinguishes two different failure modes: the 'expected cache hit' assertion (hits < 5, TTL expiry) and a TimeoutError from the backend fetch
No file under cachelib/ or tests/ was modified

evals.name: shell-step-intermittent
evals.prompt: the first step of our deploy job, `bash scripts/fetch.sh`, fails randomly in CI and we just hit retry. can you figure out how often it fails and what the errors are?
evals.expected_output: Runs the script repeatedly (>=10), reports ~25% failure, names connection reset (exit 56) as dominant; if the rarer checksum mismatch (exit 3) was sampled, reports it separately.
expectations: The script was executed at least 10 times
The final answer reports a numeric failure rate or count out of total runs
The final answer identifies 'Connection reset by peer' (curl exit 56) as the main failure

If more than one distinct error message appeared across the runs (e.g. a checksum mismatch besides the connection reset), the final answer reports them as separate failure modes with their counts rather than collapsing them into one

evals.name: deterministic-not-flaky
evals.prompt: test_total_rounding in tests/test_total.py is flaky, it fails on and off in CI. can you check how flaky it is?
evals.expected_output: Runs it repeatedly and concludes it fails every time (deterministic float rounding bug), so it is not flaky.
expectations: The test was executed more than once before concluding
The final answer concludes the failure is deterministic (fails on every run) rather than flaky, and says so explicitly
The final answer identifies float arithmetic (0.30000000000000004 != 0.3) as the cause
